newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain economy in better form than Italy - Berlusconi.
newsitem.headline: Spain economy in better form than Italy - Berlusconi.

text.p: The Spanish economy is in better shape than its Italian counterpart, Italy's right-wing opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Wednesday.
"There are fundamental economic data which are better in Spain than in Italy," he told reporters at a news conference, having met Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Tuesday.
He said Aznar's government was trying to develop the economy, similar to Berlusconi's party programme.
"Spain created 200,000 new jobs in 1996, and they are planning to increase that by another 240,000 in 1997," he said.
Berlusconi said on Tuesday he was in favour of a delay in the start of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union, adding that Italy had little chance of making the start in 1999.
"I do not think we'll be in (at the start in 1999), and if we enter we will not stay," Berlusconi said.
"It's possible to enter via creative accounting, as France did, but it's not possible to do it and remain in."
Berlusconi served as prime minister for seven months in 1994, and is now leader of the right-wing Freedom Alliance.
